![Recursive Superintelligence founders. Photo from [The New York Times](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/05/13/technology/recursive-superintelligence-funding-ai.html).](cover.jpg){fig-align="center" data-lightbox-src="cover-full.jpg"}

The New York Times [reports](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/05/13/technology/recursive-superintelligence-funding-ai.html) that Recursive Superintelligence, a stealth-mode AI lab with offices in San Francisco and London, has emerged with more than $650 million in funding at a valuation above $4 billion. The investors include [GV](https://www.gv.com/) (formerly Google Ventures), [Greycroft](https://www.greycroft.com/), [Nvidia](https://www.nvidia.com/), and [AMD](https://www.amd.com/). [Richard Socher](https://www.richard.socher.org/), CEO of [You.com](https://you.com/) and former head of AI research at Salesforce, founded the company with seven co-founders. NYT names four: [Josh Tobin](https://www.joshtobin.com/), [Jeff Clune](http://jeffclune.com/), and [Tim Shi](https://timshi.xyz/), all from OpenAI, plus [Yuandong Tian](https://yuandong-tian.com/) from Meta. The six-month-old company has fewer than 30 employees, and has separately hired [Peter Norvig](https://norvig.com/), 25-year director of research at Google and co-author of [*Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach*](https://aima.cs.berkeley.edu/), the standard university AI textbook for three decades. Long-term, the founders aim to apply the technology beyond AI itself, to drug discovery and biological research.

> A.I. is code. And now, A.I. can code. The ingredients are there.
>
> --- Richard Socher

## My Notes

- **Recursive self-improvement is becoming a funded category.** Recursive Superintelligence joins a competitive field that already includes [AMI Labs](https://ami.inc/) (world models; see Yann LeCun's [recent appearance](/posts/20260523-yann-lecun-after-llms/) for the thesis), [Ineffable Intelligence](https://www.wired.com/story/david-silver-ai-ineffable-intelligence-reinforcement-learning/) (RL, David Silver's), and [Safe Superintelligence](https://ssi.inc/) (safety-first), plus [Mirendil](https://mirendil.com/) and Anthropic's [Automated Alignment Researchers](https://www.anthropic.com/research/automated-alignment-researchers) per Jack Clark's [Import AI 455](/posts/20260508-import-ai-455-automating-ai-research/). Add to the list [Sakana AI](https://sakana.ai/), whose "AI Scientist" papers have been pushing automated research-paper production since 2024 and which Jack didn't mention. NYT also notes a separately-funded namesake (Ricursive Intelligence, also valued at $4B, also chasing recursive self-improvement) and confirms Anthropic and OpenAI are pursuing the same outcome. The category is consolidating before its first public technical milestone.

- **The founders are an open-endedness team.** NYT explicitly characterizes the team that way: "Many of these researchers specialize in a kind of AI development called 'open-endedness.' This involves building software systems that can run for days, months or even years in pursuit of goals set by the researchers." [Jeff Clune](http://jeffclune.com/) is the most public face of the lineage: [POET](https://arxiv.org/abs/1901.01753), [MAP-Elites](https://arxiv.org/abs/1504.04909), [AI-generating algorithms](https://arxiv.org/abs/1905.10985), all arguing systems should generate their own training distribution. [Yuandong Tian](https://yuandong-tian.com/) brings Meta's RL/self-play track ([OpenGo](https://github.com/pytorch/ELF), [Searchformer](https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.14083)). [Josh Tobin](https://www.joshtobin.com/) brings OpenAI robotics ([domain randomization](https://arxiv.org/abs/1703.06907), [Dactyl](https://arxiv.org/abs/1808.00177)). [Tim Shi](https://timshi.xyz/) ([Cresta](https://cresta.com/)) is the agent-deployment hand. [Peter Norvig](https://norvig.com/) gives the project the textbook-canonical AI brand.

- **OpenAI's "automated AI researcher" is the concrete benchmark.** Sam Altman [said](https://x.com/sama/status/1983584366547829073) OpenAI hopes to have a system doing the work of a "less experienced" researcher by fall 2026. Recursive Superintelligence is pitching a years-long arc instead; Socher himself told NYT the technology will need years, and the article notes that "humans like Dr. Socher must still generate the new ideas that drive AI development forward." The category's strongest tension sits in that gap between a quarter-by-quarter benchmark and a years-long bet.
